gaps.sentence: Hush! The director ___ about the budget at the moment.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows active thinking process
gaps.explanation: Here 'think' describes a mental process in progress, not an opinion, so the continuous is used: is thinking.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: They ___ so much since they started the new school.
gaps.hint: since they started with present result
gaps.explanation: Change measured from a past starting point to now takes the present perfect: have grown.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: She is exhausted because she ___ since dawn.
gaps.hint: since dawn explains her present exhaustion
gaps.explanation: An action running from the past to now and explaining a present state takes the present perfect continuous: has been travelling.

gaps.sentence: This is the second time the printer ___ down this week.
gaps.explanation: 'This is the second time …' is followed by the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.
